-some noise from the fan

-does not come with wire options for a Mac, so make sure you buy/have a cable for this. Takes USB-->HDMI, which worked great for me

text_fidelity_a:
Kodak PlayFull ZE2 Waterproof Video Camera with 2x Optical Zoom and 2-Inch LCD Screen (Black) Though I use Windows XP, my computer is old and my processor (Sempron) is not what is required to run the "KODAK Share Button" app to transfer videos from the Kodak Playful, Model Ze2 to my computer. That's too bad. But anyway, be sure to check the specs before buying so this won't happen to you. I downloaded the program anyway but it wouldn't run. So, I've tried just about everything I know to do and nothing seems to work. An old "FinePixViewer" program keeps popping up every time I try to download a video, but it takes a very long time for it to finally work. I guess technology is trying to force me to buy a newer/faster computer because so many gadgets won't work on poor ole' Bessie anymore despite her having 34 GB left of memory and 4GB of ram.

The camera itself is fun to play with and I like the 1970's film mode, but it would be better if the theme to "Shaft" was being quietly played in the background while using that particular mode. The access doors are very difficult to open and you will probably lose some fingernails until you get it figured out. The Kodak website is not very good.....I never could find a place where I could ask a question directly to technical support. And the web addresses provided in the manual take you to the same web page regardless of the the specifics written into the web address like: [...]. They all take you to the same place and you have to hunt and peck where you want to go and what you're looking for. And they have no Ze2 demos to watch - go figure. And though Windows XP is listed in a drop menu, when I click on it absolutely nothing happens. So much for Windows XP help.

I'm giving it 3 stars because the doors are a pain, and the website is inadequate. But since I don't own a computer that will allow the Kodak program to work I can't fairly judge the quality of the videos. When I can get FinePixView to play them they look alright. I have yet to connect the Kodak Playful directly to my HDTV to see how the HD (720) quality and sound are, and I will do that and report back. I am very interested especially in the sound quality since I'm a musician/music teacher and like to record my students playing.

UPDATE: 2.17.12
I used the Kodak Playful to record my daughter playing guitar in her school's talent show. It did a good job and I was finally able to upload the video to my old computer. Also, I ended up breaking off the door that covers the USB plug which was nearly impossible to open without losing fingernails and then equally impossible to shut close again. The plug stays inside without the door and though I hated doing it, it works much better now.
text_fidelity_b: Kodak PlayFull ZE2 Waterproof Video Camera with 2x Optical Zoom and 2-Inch LCD Screen (Black)

While signal strength from my Linksys router is good in most rooms, there’s a few areas (such as the basement) where the signal is so weak that maintaining a connection fast enough to stream movies is problematic (spend lots of time looking at the “buffering” message from Netflix). Using this as a repeater has solved that problem.

It’s very compact – the whole router plugs right into the wall and is about the same size as a typical USB charger or similar device. The indicator lights for network connectivity and data transfer are on the front, but are dim enough that they don’t cause a problem at night.

The only notable negative is that the instructions are spotty at best. Getting this up and running is not a problem if you have experience in router setup, but could be tough if you’ve never done it before.

Although I'm using this only as a repeater, it offers additional functionality. It can be used in router mode so it functions as a router, or WISP mode, where it rebroadcasts a wireless network under a different name. I can't speak to how it works in modes other than repeater, but given it's excellent repeater functionality, I would imagine other modes work just as well.

With the exception of the instructions, zero problems with this. It’s a very effective (and compact) solution to extending WiFi coverage. Highly recommend.

RayHom 8 Bay AA AAA Battery Charger, Double Charging Speed with LCD Display Independent Slot for Ni-MH AA AAA Rechargeable Batteries This is a nice alternative to chargers that require you to charge batteries in pairs. There are spaces for eight batteries, and you can charge any number within them, and mix and match AA and AAA. The eight spaces are divided electrically into two banks of four spaces, and the manufacturer says each bank can provide 2000 mA of charging power (which lowers as you add more batteries and the current is divided between them). However, the included adapter only provides only 1200 mA (so says its label), so I'm not sure the math checks out.

I gave it a test with an assortment of different brand and capacity rechargeables, then checked the batteries with a multimeter. Even fully loaded the charger worked pretty quickly and brought each one up to just over 1.4 volts. I have a brand-name charger that will bring them up to 1.5 volts, but that may be overcharging a bit and might reduce overall battery life.

The one minor negative is that the battery icons on the backlit display are pretty much invisible unless you bend down or tilt the charger up to see them. You can see how low the angle is in the photo I uploaded.

Other than that, convenient and reasonably fast, it's a nice charger.

text_fidelity_a:
Kindle Oasis E-reader with Leather Charging Cover - Black, 6" High-Resolution Display (300 ppi), Wi-Fi + Free Cellular Connectivity, Built-In Audible (Previous Generation - 8th) I've been an avid fan of ebooks since the long gone days of the Rocket and the eBookman, and a fan of the Kindle since the very beginning. This is miles and away the best there has ever been. It is a luxury model, no doubt, but oh is it luxurious.

I like:
The weight. Even in the case it's very light, though if it gets much lighter I'll worry about it blowing away in a strong wind.
The size. It's not going to get much smaller without shrinking the screen.
The interface. I'm sorry, I like buttons. Call me old. I never bent back the spine of a book (horrors) so I can't compare the feel of this to that, but I can say it's nice for a long reading session. The touch screen takes a bit of getting used to, but the tutorial will guide a new user. The tutorial is intrusive at first, but provides useful information and goes away quickly. I will suggest customizing the screen. I hated the default, but you get a lot of options to make it just the way you want.
The lighting is now all but invisible. I was unhappy that you can't completely turn it off as you could with the Nook Glowlight, and turning it down casts an odd yellow light over the page, but it's so even now as to be so unintrusive I barely notice going from sunlight to tunnel on the bus home. With the Nook I'd be thrown out of the book to go turn on the light. With the Kindle, I can keep reading without a pause. It does not have adaptive lighting, but I'm not sure it needs it.
The download speed. I don't know if it's supposed to be faster than the Kindle Keyboard (the last one I had with 3G) but it certainly seems that way.
The battery life. Maybe with this thing going for months we'll finally hear an end to the "but my dead tree doesn't run out of power" nonsense.
Next in series. When you're almost done with a book, it tells you where the story continues. Now the next feature I want, and if it does this I haven't seen it yet, is an alert when the next book in a series I'm following is published. Yes, FictFact is great, but I'm greedy and want it right on the device.

I don't like:
It's not waterproof. There was a lot of hope it would be after the Nook went that route.
It's not solar, yet, but there are rumors of a solar cover coming soon.
It doesn't support Audible and the excellent immersive reading between ebook and audiobook. I have a weird love of that feature, seeing what changed print to audio.
Recommended Content and Reading Lists. I shut this feature off. The information seems scattered at best and gave me no useful information, especially considering how precious screen real estate is.
text_fidelity_b: Kindle Oasis E-reader with Leather Charging Cover - Black, 6" High-Resolution Display (300 ppi), Wi-Fi + Free Cellular Connectivity, Built-In Audible (Previous Generation - 8th)

text_fidelity_a:
Walker Edison Wren Classic 4 Cubby TV Stand for TVs up to 65 Inches, 58 Inch, Dark Walnut First off, at this price point 3-stars is pretty good, but compared with the reviews and what I expected, there are a few things that bother me. First off, of course the corner damage comes on the top piece of wood... even if they packed that piece upside down it would be improved by not having the damage on the showing corner. So have to live with an unsightly corner, because not going to repackage this thing and try to return it. Secondly the tolerances on the construction were not great... an eighth-inch here, failing to line up well there, nothing tragic, but all in all was not as high quality as other bargain furniture like that company that sounds like leek. And while construction was easy and fast, there are a couple of simple things they could have done (this end up/ arrow stickers) that would have made things 10x simpler, as it was I had to back out of 3 different steps because one of the pieces was backwards, and I generally consider myself good at these things. The wiring cutout circles on the back panel are not well placed, should be lower and so they are too easy to see and unsightly even with equipment in place.

The final product is pretty rectangular boxy with it's prominent right angles, especially in the middle... I do not know quite how to describe it, but now that I have experienced it and I look at these photos here, I should have seen it. In our room- which features smoother lines- it just looks a little too boxy. Finally, I was hoping the accent colors in the furniture would be better aligned to the existing woods in our room, but there are no synergies, tended to be very washed out grays, which is in fact what they are advertising anyway, but since their photos do not feature other natural woods, was hard to gauge.

One high point is that because of the lighter shade of this unit, it really disappears under the television, rather than calling attention to itself.

I would not hesitate to recommend- again at this price point it is hard to gripe, but if I could do it over, I would spend more on a nicer piece.
text_fidelity_b: Walker Edison Wren Classic 4 Cubby TV Stand for TVs up to 65 Inches, 58 Inch, Dark Walnut

Epson VS230 SVGA 3LCD Projector, 2800 Lumens Color Brightness I also have an Epson EX7220 WXGA projector with 3000/3000 color/white lumens. Both are excellent projectors that have surprised me by their ease of use and great clarity even in lit rooms. But the EX7220 costs about 50% more, while the two projectors come in the exact same form factor (i.e., the casing, buttons, and remote are 99.5% identical). Additionally, there are loads of other Epson projectors in their lineup, all priced differently, so what do you get when you spend more money?

1) Resolution. I just now realized how important this is. Although I was surprised just how well both projectors play movies from my computer projected onto a wall (even a light yellow or a light brown wall, without the color of the picture seeming to suffer), I now realize that you should pick a resolution that matches your computer's resolution or your computer's ability to send out the projector's native resolution.

For example, my computer's native resolution is WXGA and so is the EX7220's, so I can mirror my monitor's image on the wall (which is what you'll probably do in most situations - especially presentations - so you can see what is happening on your small screen. The alternative is to "extend" your desktop onto the wall, which in some cases can output a different resolution, but this is not as practical in most cases, particularly presentations) with a perfect match from computer to projector. However, when I connect the VS330 in XGA resolution (with a 4:3 ratio), it looks good, but there is black, unused space all around the actual image because the resolutions are in different formats. The black area is basically wasted pixels. You can put it in 4:3 mode, but you're getting a degraded (although still sharp) image on the wall.

Just as monitors have gotten higher in resolution over time, projectors are not far behind. But you definitely pay for the difference. For basic work presentations and casual video watching, 1024x768 is fine. As you want to put more information on one screen or watch high definition movies in your free time, you'll want to look at a higher end monitor.

2. Luminescence. There is now an official standard to differentiate between color lumens and white lumens, whereas in the past only lumens were specified. I am fully convinced that color lumens matter, particularly for presentations where visual content matters and especially for video watching. That said, I am amazed how great movies look projected onto a large, empty wall, and it surprises me that more people don't watch everything via projector. I'd never buy a projector that didn't specify color lumens. And, clearly, you pay exponentially for a greater color lumen output.

3. Accessories. The VS330 lacks the carry bag, wireless connection dongle (although it comes with the bracket that now I have to be sure not to lose in case I'd ever get the dongle), and extra cables that come with the EX7220. Not a big deal by any standards, although I do like the (very basic) carry bag that comes with the EX7220.

To speak specifically to this projector, I am really impressed how easy it is to set up and get working correctly. It's basically plug and play, eliminating most of the risk of those embarrassing moments where no one can get the projector to work. Most of the functionality also comes through the remote as well. You can also put the sound through the projector, and I love the retractable tilting foot on the device. It's small, boots up quickly, is easy to use, and is really impressive with its picture, even for playing movies. That's a great side benefit, but as you start looking into its use as a movie machine, that's where you really start looking at higher end models, and it's hard to know where to stop, because they make a few models much more geared toward movies well beyond the EX7220.

This is a great machine. I'd recommend Epson to anyone based on my experience. As for which model to buy, I'd tell you to take a careful look at your needs. This model is great for ease of use and quality of picture for basic office uses.
text_fidelity_b: Epson VS230 SVGA 3LCD Projector, 2800 Lumens Color Brightness

text_fidelity_a:
Ring Video Doorbell 3 – enhanced wifi, improved motion detection, easy installation Great wireless camera/doorbell. Hardware/software this is ideal. We live on a busy street so we were getting lots of notifications. The software allowed us to adjust where the camera sensed motion, cutting down "false" notifications. Easy to use.
Easy to setup and install. Took maybe 15 minutes from opening the box to having it up and running.
Convenient set-up and access via phone (iOS and Android) app. Added skill to Echo, so when someone sets of camera or pushes doorbell, we get a notification via Alexa, and an image on the Echo show. You can adjust how often and what notifications you receive in the app.
Night vision is pretty good as well. Another nice feature is you can access a "live" view anytime, notification or not.
Audio works well, so if you are in the basement, garage, at work, shopping you can talk to whomever is at your door.
If you carry your phone everywhere or have a smart home speaker (Google, Echo or maybe Apple?) you won't need the additional chime, phone and speakers have a decently loud sound.
I would suggest getting a second battery if you have a busy street or lots of activity. The app notifies you in plenty of time the battery is low and needs to be recharged (only takes a couple hours to fully charge). But a second battery extends the life and less work (but to be fair, one screw using included driver, slide off plate, slide battery out, set to charge and reverse process to put battery back in. With two batteries, the whole thing takes about two minutes. With one, you simply have a non-functioning doorbell/camera for a few hours. No biggie, just FYI.
Also there is an an App called Neighbors free to join and use. It lets you share "videos and notifications of criminal or suspicious activity. So if someone in your neighborhood is broken into or home is vandalized they can share the video and/or share a notice of the incident. Lost dog, share. Delivery thieves, share. So both kinda cool and scary.
Now the BAD. To access the video you have to pay a monthly fee ( now if you access the video within the first 30 seconds or so, you are golden, but if you have your hands full, or can't access your phone, you can't see the video, or back it up. While the basic few is like $40 ish a year. Higher for the next tier up. That is forever. And no easy way to back up to a local storage device. All files are on Rings servers.
Now if you know that up front, and $40 is no biggie. Then 5 stars.
But for me that is an issue.
text_fidelity_b: Ring Video Doorbell 3 – enhanced wifi, improved motion detection, easy installation

text_fidelity_a:
Epica Digital Emergency Solar Hand Crank AM/FM/NOAA Radio, Flashlight, Smartphone Charger with NOAA Certified Weather Alert & Cable-ONE Cable Does All This is one of those products that is good to have, but even better if you never need to use it since you'll probably be using it when the electricity is out. It offers a lot of functionality in a compact size: a flashlight, AM radio, FM radio and weather band radio. It runs off of an internal rechargeable battery that is kept charged either via solar power, USB connection or by cranking the handle. It can also serve as a source to charge a cell phone (albeit with very limited capacity to do so since the internal battery is only rated at 800mAh).

It works pretty well. The flashlight is very bright - had no problems lighting my way down a dark stairway and in a totally dark room. The radio is OK. The reception is spotty and it only picked up a few of the very strong stations in the area. It's very susceptible to positioning - moving it just a couple of inches turned a clear station into static.

Cranking the handle to keep it charged is pretty easy. It turns easily and the handle is comfortable. According to the manual, one minute of cranking equals 30 minutes of flashlight use or 20 minutes of radio use.

This is a good product to keep on hand in case of emergency, such as a bad storm or extended power outage. It won't keep you cool in the summer or warm in the winter, but at least you can see where you're going and listen to the radio. Definitely worth a spot in the emergency kit. The only shortcoming is the somewhat limited radio reception.
[sample provided by manufacturer for review]
text_fidelity_b: Epica Digital Emergency Solar Hand Crank AM/FM/NOAA Radio, Flashlight, Smartphone Charger with NOAA Certified Weather Alert & Cable-ONE Cable Does All

text_fidelity_a:
Garmin 010-01689-00 Forerunner 35; Easy-to-Use GPS Running Watch, Black I did a good amount of research on other devices before buying this product. I initially wanted a sleek smartwatch that also had great fitness tracking modes, but apparently you either get a pretty smartwatch/OK fitness tracker, or a decent fitness tracker/outdated looking smartwatch. In the end I decided I wanted mainly a fitness tracker that has some smartwatch features, and that I wouldn't use most of the features on an actual smartwatch.

PROS

The app is awesome! My husband is a software developer so I learn a lot about what makes good apps good and what makes bad apps bad. This app is free and user friendly. It has mostly accurate measurements and you can easily track your progress and areas of improvement. It also has a feature that allows whoever you send the link to to track your location, in case you are concerned about getting kidnapped on your run. Very good stuff.

The steps I get seem to be pretty consistent as well as the distance traveled. The heartrate tracker seems to be mostly accurate (checked with manual pulse check).

The battery life is pretty good. Obviously I would use more battery if I am using the fitness modes. Depending on your activity level and use of the fitness modes, the battery could last you all week plus some. The battery charges to full in about 30 minutes.

I like the rectangular watch face and the light green band. I also like that you can change the bands. Apparently for some of the expensive FitBit models the band is not changeable so some people just buy a whole new watch. Like whaaat?

CONS
I like being able to see the texts I get on the watch, but I don't really care for receiving phone calls (I get so many spam calls that I don't even answer my phone lol). I don't think there is a way to say 'no' to having phone calls, so I get frequent notifications to enable phone call permissions. It's not too much of a problem but it's kind of annoying sometimes.

I think the sleep tracker is interesting, but I don't think it is accurate. I think that as long as you are "resting" during the hours that you put as your sleeping hours under Settings, that it considers this as sleep. Sometimes I can't sleep but the device considers this as light sleep. I think this would be an interesting addition, that perhaps it could be integrated: I am a night shift worker and I switch between day/night sleep, so I have to manually enter my bedtimes in the app's User Settings to sleep. I think that if there was an activity button, like when you choose walk/run/cardio on the watch itself, for sleep, it would be easier for me personally. I am not sure if that could be done with a software update or if this is a hardware type thing.

FINAL THOUGHTS

I wear this watch almost 24/7 and I think it has helped me consider and evaluate my activity levels as well as track my improvement. I think that if Garmin made a watch that had the aesthetics and watch interface comparable to the Apple watch but kept the good fitness aspect, I would definitely purchase as an upgrade.
text_fidelity_b: Garmin 010-01689-00 Forerunner 35; Easy-to-Use GPS Running Watch, Black

text_fidelity_a:
Bluetooth Speaker with LCD Display, NFC, FM Radio and Subwoofer Effect- Shower Speaker with Crystal Clear Sound and 3 Firm Suction Cups – Hands Free Speakerphone … (Red) [[VIDEOID:413906e1ac04fb2e066baa4adca5a20a]] This Bluetooth Shower Speaker with LCD Display by Abco Tech is the first shower speaker I've ever tried, so I can't compare it to any other one. I can share my impression of it from the perspective of one who hasn't used this sort of product before though and I hope that will be helpful to some of you who also haven't tried one before.

First of all, it measures 5 x 5 x 5 inches, and needs to be charged by USB after you receive it. Once it's charged you can attach it to a non-porous surface via three large suction cups in the rear of the speaker. We weren't able to get it to stick to our tile but it did attach firmly to the inside of the glass shower door and has held for three days so far without slipping or falling despite opening and closing the door.

The control buttons are easy to understand and operate. When you turn it on it makes a fairly loud beep, then the LCD display turns on and displays the time. I find having the clock very useful when trying to get kids out of the shower in time for school by the way! It has an integrated FM radio and you can preset up to 10 of your favorite stations and switch between them easily using the rewind and fast forward buttons. If you want to find different stations it will also do seek. When you select the radio mode it beeps loudly once again and then plays the station. Reception varies depending on signal strength, weather conditions and all the usual reasons. The default sound level is high but it's easy to adjust using the control buttons on the speaker.

Bluetooth: We had no problem pairing it to my daughter's iPhone 4S and streaming Pandora. In fact, the sound quality is excellent we thought! Once again the default sound level is high, but you can adjust that with the control buttons. ** It seemed as though we had problems getting it to switch to Bluetooth in the video, but that was because my daughter forgot to turn her phone back on for a moment. Once she did you can hear how good it sounded.** When you get a phone call while listening to the speaker it displays the calling phone number so you can decide whether to take the call or not, and if you decide to take it the speaker acts as a speakerphone.

Charge: So far it's been up for three days and we haven't had to charge it again, but then again we're only using it when in the shower or bathroom for longer periods of time so length of time it will hold the charge will vary depending on your usage. The rubber charging port cover doesn't want to stay covering the port up though, but it doesn't appear to have an effect on the speaker working.

We're very pleased by the quality, sound quality, and the features offered by this Bluetooth shower speaker so far. If anything changes I will update this review. I did receive a retail sample provided for evaluation and review consideration. I hope being able to see the actual speaker in position and working helps you to make a better informed buying decision. If you have any questions feel free to ask them in the comments section below and I'll try to respond as soon as I can. :)
text_fidelity_b: Bluetooth Speaker with LCD Display, NFC, FM Radio and Subwoofer Effect- Shower Speaker with Crystal Clear Sound and 3 Firm Suction Cups – Hands Free Speakerphone … (Red)

text_fidelity_a:
Dell Venue 7 16 GB Tablet (Android) This is a great tablet for the money. It is sturdy, lightweight, and easy to use.

The tablet has a good weight for its size. It featues a 7 inch screen, the back of the devise smooth matte black with the Dell logo on it.

The power button is on the top right, Volume rocker buttons are on the left along with the micro USB port (used for charging with the included charger or for connecting to your computer) The right has an expansion slot for a micro SD card.

It runs Android 4.2.2. If you are at all familiar with Android this will be a snap. I have a Samsung Galaxy and they are pretty much identical in the way they operate. Only difference is the slight additions that Samsung adds to their phone operating system user interface. The system is pretty clear of bloatware, so there are very few apps that usually come preloaded on your phones.

Setup is easy. Answer a few questions and you are off and running. If you have a google account (gmail, google plus) you enter that and you can begin downloading apps you've previously downloaded on our phone or purchased.

The system runs very smooth and fast. It boots in under 30 seconds. Switching screens, loading apps, and opening menus is blazingly fast. It is really really fast.

The screen is very bright and can be viewed at some intense angles and it looks very good.

The front facing camera is decent, though not excellent. It comes in at about 3 megapixels, pretty good for taking photos. They are a bit grainy, though passable. Definable will not replace your regular camera. The rear facing camera is not good at all, you will not be taking very good selfies with this. It is passable, though, for doing things like Skype or participating in a Google hangout or video conference it will do a good job because you usually don't want to broadcast on too high a resolution anyway.

Most any google apps will run on this. I've seen no problems or incompatible apps. I've used Netflix, Hula, Pandora, and others. They load fast and multimedia looks good.

This does not run flash! So if you want to view sits like Amazon streaming movies you will have a hard time. I am looking for a workaround, but as of writing this have not found one.

The sound quality is very good. the speakers are on the bottom and they sound pretty good. There is a headphone/data port on the top. So you can listen to music with headphones or use an input device such as a credit card reader like I have with the Square Register app or with headphone/microphone devices.

Battery life is good. If you are using it hard, you'll have to charge it every evening, though if you use it here and there, you can get a few days out of it.

It also has Bluetooth connectivity and it has worked well connecting to my various devices. Wireless is fast and easy to set up

The only weird thing is the micro USB cord seems to be upside down. That is though the plug fits in snugly to the device, it seems contrary to what you expect. I'm always trying to put the USB connector in upside down. Just kind of funny and does not diminish the device.

Overall a sturdy capable tablet. Runs very fast, good battery life, clear screen, and good sound. Will run most any app you'd care to run. If you are familiar with Android, you'll have no problems using this and it'll seem like old hat. Very easy to learn, setup, and use.

I highly recommend!!

UPDATE!!:: As of December 19th, 2013 there is an OS upgrade. This now runs Android 4.3. If you have this already and it is NOT running 4.3, go to Settings/About Tablet/system updates
text_fidelity_b: Dell Venue 7 16 GB Tablet (Android)

text_fidelity_a:
Kindle Fire - Includes Special Offers (Previous Generation - 2nd) I just received my kindle fire today. I had a hard time deciding between the HD, this, and the paperwhite. I decided on this one, because I really thought I'd like the immersion reading. I have an audible account and I've been reading along to the audiobooks. It's amazing how fast I can get through the books (at 3x speed) and I really retain the info. The immersion reading is super-easy to use and definitely worth upgrading to this. The whole point of the kindle is to read more, and this new feature makes it possible to read 2 or 3 times as many books in the same amount of time. I'm an average-speed reader and was able to read 4 books (with the help of the audiobook reading pace) in the last 30 days and one was the 800+ page Stephen king, "11/22/63".

I also tested out the text to speech. It's a lady's voice and much, much, easier to understand than the text to speech on my kindle keyboard. It also has many speed options and I think it reads faster than my kindle keyboard version. I am very, very pleased with it.

It is much more responsive than the previous kindle fire I'm upgrading from.

If you are worried about the free offers, don't be. I DETEST commercials and advertising so much, I quit reading magazines and watching television. The offers only show on the startup, no big deal. I already took advantage of a $5.00 credit for amazon video. I was able to rent two movies and it only cost me 89 cents, when it was said and done, and I was planning on renting Hunger Games tonight, anyway. So, so far, I don't mind the offers at all.

My favorite feature is the immersion reading and the text-to-speech improvements. I also downloaded all the free kindle books with the free audiobooks for the immersion experience. These are books I always wanted to read,but never had the discipline to just read them. Reading and listening to those books are worth the price of this new gadget, IMO.

Way to go, Amazon, for a great product and a great price!

P.S.
I have an iPad, and the last time I went on vacation, I left it at home and brought only my fire and kindle keyboard. I didn't miss my iPad at all and this new gen fire is even better. Seriously, it's that good.

3. Dump this modem and try another one

text_fidelity_a:
SiriusXM Onyx Plus Satellite Radio w/ Vehicle Kit, Enjoy SiriusXM Through your Existing Car Stereo for as Low as $5/month + $60 Service Card with Activation So let's start out with that it's a nice step up from your standard car radio. I like the overall design and you can save up to 20 channels and have 5 saved stations that you can tune into to transmit your signal, which I find nice for those areas when you start picking up other radio stations and there is bleed through. I didn't realize this at first, but the radio does have an internal transmitter, though I don't know if having it directly plugged into a transmitter will make any difference. So far mine has done nicely without the help of a third party transmitter. The little screen is nice too. It is not a touch screen, but you can see it well during the daytime and I find that for me the brightness at night is just right, not super blinding bright, but not so dim that you can't see it either. The radio also works similar to DVR and you can rewind to play a song again.

Set up is fairly easy and the instructions are easy to follow as well. I'd say it may take 30 minutes to an hour tops to set it up (that includes tucking away cords and positioning it where you want it) and activating it.

It does not come with a remote, but I think it would improve the experience of going through the channels, especially when driving, so you can still keep your eyes on the road and change the channel if you are wanting something different from your presets. Also, I believe you have to have a Sirius dock/boom box of sorts if you want to bring it inside and play music. You can transfer this radio between cars too, depending on your setup though, you may want to have a secondary dock and antenna set up in the second vehicle so its easier to transition and your not having to drag the dock and accessories around from car to car.

Something to take into consideration if you are thinking of getting this radio or other xm radios is that if you are not familiar with the subscription charges, is that you will have to pay the subscription fee, your state tax and a royalty fee and there is an activation fee. So outside of tax, I didn't realize there were other charges with the subscription fee. Personally I went with the 10.99 subscription and my fees were estimated to be 14.99 (this will probably vary from location to location), so not too much extra on regular fees after the activation fee. Just something to know so your not caught by surprise.

If its really cloudy or if you are under something like a metal awning/covering, the signal will go out.

I think the only thing that I don't like about the radio is the antenna. The reason I don't like the antenna is because the cord is too long for how I use it. I keep the antenna inside my car and the signal works fine, but the cord is ridiculously long. It could be upgraded to a motorcycle antenna, which is about 8 inches long, compared to X amount of feet. For others this won't be a problem, because you may need every bit of that extra cord, so it just depends on how you plan to set it up.
text_fidelity_b: SiriusXM Onyx Plus Satellite Radio w/ Vehicle Kit, Enjoy SiriusXM Through your Existing Car Stereo for as Low as $5/month + $60 Service Card with Activation

text_fidelity_a:
Amazon Basics Wireless Bluetooth Fitness Headphones Earbuds with Microphone, Black Short story of the review is that these are just as they say they are--a pair of relatively inexpensive "basic" earphones. As such, they seem to be a decent value and have some good points, but if you're looking for sound quality over price, you'll want to go elsewhere.

Pros:
Packaging: small and minimalist as it should be

Provided with: multiple size earbuds caps and ear inserts (more on these later), a very short charging cable, and a decent zip-around traveling pouch

Pairing: No problem with any of my Apple devices. Instantly recognized and paired with an iPhone (8 and 6), iPad (Pro and Air 2), and MacBook Pro. Couldn't be quicker or easier each and every time

Comfort: This was an issue for me, though obviously this is a pretty subjective category. I had to step down immediately to the small caps/rings, which is no surprise--I do that with I think all of my earbuds. But even with the smalls I just couldn't get a a good seal or a comfortable, though oddly enough much worse with my right. The left was not "great" but was certainly good; right was a bad seal and wholly uncomfortable no matter what I tried. Weird.

Sound quality: Again, it's a matter of pricing here. I don't own many basics and it's been years since I've had a set of lower-tier earbuds, so it's hard for me to compare at an equal level. The sound is what I'd call adequate, especially for exercise or listening to an audiobook. But there's no comparison to my PowerBeats3 or Jaybird X2s, and not even to my Jabra Elites, which I"d call my mid-range ones. The first two are in a whole other class in terms of range, sharpness, richness, and comfort, while the Jabras are a good step up in both sound and comfort. Sound here is more than a little thin at both ends, and just not very rich or full. Less noticeable with an audiobook, but definitely not the buds I'd choose if I'm focusing on listening to music, as opposed to having background sound while I"m doing something else. Phone quality is pretty similar--adequate, at times a bit muddy.

Controls: easy, intuitive, and responsive

Overall, if you want a basic set where quality of sound isn't a deal breaker, or a pair of cheaper ones for places you might have to worry about forgetting them, these will suit the bill, assuming you don't have the same comfort issue I did. But for someone looking for rich, full sound, particularly for music, I'd strongly advise moving up the ladder
text_fidelity_b: Amazon Basics Wireless Bluetooth Fitness Headphones Earbuds with Microphone, Black

text_fidelity_a:
Coby Kyros 7-Inch Android 2.3 4 GB Internet Touchscreen Tablet - MID7012-4G (Black) I never owned a tablet or a smartphone so I suppose if I did my review might be different but I think this is a pretty neat little tablet and the price is pretty great too.

I've had it for a couple of days and downloaded the Amazon App store which has most of the apps anyone could need. I mean seriously how many apps does an average person really use? I have downloaded quite a few games for both myself and my kids, the Kindle app, I heart Radio app, and the US newspaper app. So far its holding all of it but I also ordered a microsdhc card for extra space to hold more apps and e-books. I have a regular Kindle that I've had for quite a few years and I am able to transfer most of the books onto this tablet also (I haven't tried downloading all of them since my son uses a few for school). It has where you can calibrate the stylus. Also if you longpress the stylus onto the wallpaper it will let you change the wallpaper in the background.

It does not come with a camera and flashplayer is not installed (but what I understand you can install a "lite" version of flashplayer which I have not done as of yet). The touchscreen is more geared toward using the stylus (which is included) which is a let down to some people. You can use your fingertip but it isn't as responsive as with the stylus IMO. It also comes with a sleeve (that has a place for your stylus) and earphones. There is a charger and a USB cable. There is another cable which I'm not sure exactly what its for (sorry). I haven't used the other cables just yet (except the charger of course). As for battery life it does seem like it runs down pretty quickly (perhaps 3-4 hours). Of course, that may change depending on the type of apps you have running. I know a lot of people worry about reading books from this rather than the Kindle type e-ink. I, personally, like reading at night before I go to sleep and with the Kindle I had to keep a lamp on just to see the page..(barely)...whereas this isn't like that (my eyes are much happier!) You can change the brightness of the screen if you are worried about the brightness bothering your eyes.

I have my email accessible to the Coby Kyros so I can check it throughout the day since my daughter takes off with my laptop quite often. I also downloaded the Dolphin mini browser which I like better than the browser sent with the Kyros. It comes with the GetJar app store which has quite a few apps but Amazon has more.

Of course, I cannot guarantee how well it will hold up because I've only had it for a couple of days but overall its a nice simple little tablet. I've seen the reviews of more expensive tablets and I don't want to spend $400 on a tablet that's rated two stars. I was willing to take the chance and so far I'm happy with my purchase. I rated it 4 stars because the speaker is kinda crappy...I haven't tried listening to the radio with earphones...hopefully it sounds better. And also I wish that it was easier to install flash (I've been looking on the internet but it seems like you have to be really a techie to do it...and I'm not!) It's not an Ipad (or Ipod) so you can't rate this tablet against a product like that (of course it's half the price of a Ipod touch).
text_fidelity_b: Coby Kyros 7-Inch Android 2.3 4 GB Internet Touchscreen Tablet - MID7012-4G (Black)

I figured that even if the Orbi did not work out, the EX7500 would be helpful with my then-current setup (four Apple wifi routers that could barely cover my home).

The jury is still out on the Orbi system, as I have had to reset it a couple of times already, and it does not play all that well with all of my smart devices. BUT the EX7500 is a trouper. I have not had to do one thing to this extender beyond plugging it in and setting it up once. Setup itself was easy and took under five minutes. Adding it to the Orbi network increased my speed in the farthest ranges of my house by a good 50-75 Mbps.

I've had other extenders that, for example, gave me duplicate IP address errors and/or constantly snatched my wifi connection. My Apple extenders let excluded MAC addresses onto my network unless I duplicated those settings for each extender. This one runs completely invisibly. It's probably the most troublefree extender I've ever owned. Seriously. It is wicked expensive, but it is the one piece of networking equipment I currently own, including my Apple setup and the Orbi, that I can definitely say that I am keeping.

Winegard FL-55YR FlatWave Amplified Razor Thin HDTV Indoor Antenna (Renewed) I bought the amped FlatWave refurbished because it was $25 cheaper than a new one, and I am quite pleased with it. It DID come with gunk on it from where the previous owner had taped it up, but the gunked-up side (the black) was the one I placed against the window, facing outside, where nobody is going to see it anyway.

We live in an apartment complex on the outskirts of a city with another apartment building sitting right in front of us where the antenna would face the closest transmission tower. The first time I scanned for channels, I just laid the antenna flat on the table next to the TV. I got 14 channels on that scan (the networks often transmit more than one, so those were ABC, NBC, CBS, and Fox with their variants, one of which was CW). I moved the antenna to the center of my window, which I didn't like the looks of, and got 20 channels when I rescanned, three of which were PBS variants I hadn't gotten before; the rest were shopping channels that I don't care to receive anyway. I moved the antenna over to the side of the window with the cord side up close to the edge of the sill so the cord would hang up against the wall and not look ugly, and I got 17 channels; all I lost were those shopping channels.

We have cable in our bedrooms but none in the living room, so that's where I set up this antenna. I'm hoping I can convince DP to drop cable at some point, because it's ridiculous how much we're paying for it. We could afford to travel some if we could cut back to just internet. But sometimes you just want to be able to watch TV....
text_fidelity_b: Winegard FL-55YR FlatWave Amplified Razor Thin HDTV Indoor Antenna (Renewed)

Yamaha Audio SR-C20A Compact Sound Bar with Built-in Subwoofer and Bluetooth This SR-C20A is an entry-level Yamaha soundbar made for the smaller room and bedroom. The attraction to this model was the 3rd speaker, a powered subwoofer.

Most compact soundbars create bass through passive radiators integral with the bar … i.e. 2 powered speakers separated in width by a baffled tube radiating through holes. So, there is no controllable bass other than passive baffle sound effects.

The SR-C20A has a controllable powered subwoofer and a dual baffle radiator combined to deliver controllable high, medium, and low tones. There are five modes: standard, stereo, game, movie, and a virtual surround mode. I just picked the one that sounds best. The virtual surround provides a sense of depth and separation to my hearing.

The SR-C20A soundbar replaced a no-name 2-speaker with baffles. The difference is sizable sound improvement.

Easy install, lots of input options.

Better sound than expected. Impressive sound. Sized for the smaller room LCD/OLEAD TV. Priced right.
text_fidelity_b: Yamaha Audio SR-C20A Compact Sound Bar with Built-in Subwoofer and Bluetooth

Bose Portable Home Speaker with Alexa Voice Control Built-in Portable Home Speaker Charging Cradle, Black This is a great speaker! It has great Bose sound and gets loud!!!!
The speaker is very well packaged.
The cable has the same usbc plug in both sides. I will be buying the additional dock unit so I can just grab and go and not have to unplug it every time I want to take it somewhere.
The speaker requires the Bose Music app.
There isn’t much instructions that come with the actual speaker - it’s all online.
I already have the Bose Music app and was hoping I could just use all the settings I have already set up for another speaker - but it didn’t let me do that.
The actual setup process took me about 20 minutes.
The touch pad is very responsive and the voice pickup is great!
I don’t have to yell at it like some of my other devices!
The presets are available on the app and are pretty easy to setup. I set them up using both Amazon Music and Pandora.
In the Alexa app the Bose speaker is found under the Echo & Alexa group. It’s currently not able to be added to a speaker group as it’s treated more like a speaker than an Alexa. Hopefully an app update will change to allow this.
I also have a Bose Revolve (original) and Bose Home Speaker 300.
I am able to sync this speaker and the Home Speaker 300 through Apple Airplay 2 and the Bose Music app but this hasn’t been possible through the Alexa app.
This portable speaker has the same great sound as my Home 300 speaker. When they are playing next to each other they are in sync and make for great whole house sound.
Overall this is a great speaker with great sound and Alexa works perfectly! The setup was pretty minimal and it’s easy to use.
I like this speaker over my original Bose Revolve as I like the handle and I like to be able to tell Alexa to do things while I’m outside.
One issue I have is really with the app. I can’t seem to change the WiFi connection to the speaker without deleting the speaker from the Bose Music app.
I can change the name but not the WiFi.
I feel like I should be able to carry this speaker anywhere and connect to a friend’s WiFi or the WiFi of a guest house easily. The current way the software is set up, that’s not possible. I’m hoping there will be a software update in the future to fix this. Until then I’ll just have to use Bluetooth at those locations.
This was a little disappointing but nothing I can’t work around and doesn’t change the greatness of this speaker.
text_fidelity_b: Bose Portable Home Speaker with Alexa Voice Control Built-in Portable Home Speaker Charging Cradle, Black

ZAGG InvisibleShield HD – EZ Apply Film Screen Protector for Apple iPad Air/iPad Air 2 - Wet Apply, Clear TL;DR— not worth the extra cost, it will break and the lifetime warranty is a scam (website doesn’t work, always out of stock), just order a cheaper one and replace— IF you can somehow get Zagg to honor the warranty they will charge you at least $7 to send you a new one when this breaks (and it will def. break)

This was a great screen protector for the several months it lasted before cracking. That partially justifies the steep price tag compared to other screen protectors— but not really.

After I purchased this from amazon I registered this product on the Zagg website, which is necessary to potentially claim a replacement through the “lifetime” warranty program. When it broke, I logged back into their website to order a replacement. The first thing that was annoying was they had a message saying any product ordered within a several years long period would need to be re-registered after they had redesigned their website— my screen protector did not fall into this category, but I assume many people were out of luck on their warranties since they probably no longer had their receipts from screen protectors they had already registered. There was no email or anything warning consumers of this issue, although it’s possible it went out to only the affected people.

When I tried to order a replacement for my broken screen protector I got an error message telling me to try again later. Then the screen protector was out of stock. Then the website is down for maintenance. Then it was out of stock again. The Zagg screen protector on my phone is also broken and also had a warranty. Between the two I have been unable to order a replacement despite trying many, many times. I‘m not a computer engineer or anything, but my computer literacy is usually sufficient to navigate consumer websites. I’m pretty sure the issue is not with me, and if I am doing something wrong it’s because they have intentionally made their website impossible to navigate.

Eventually I gave up and just replaced the screen protector on my phone with a cheaper one. I was able to buy 2 new screen protectors for the same price as the SHIPPING for what the warranty replacement for the Zagg screen protector would have been if it was ever in stock when their website was working, and the difference in quality is negligible.

I don’t appreciate paying extra for a warranty that is not honored and having my time wasted trying to order a replacement when it’s clearly designed to be impossible. I also ended up keeping a broken screen protector on my phone and iPad for months while trying over and over again to order my replacement since it was under warranty.
text_fidelity_b: ZAGG InvisibleShield HD – EZ Apply Film Screen Protector for Apple iPad Air/iPad Air 2 - Wet Apply, Clear

text_fidelity_a:
K&F Concept 49mm UV CPL Lens Filter Kit 18 Multi Layer Coatings Circular Polarizer Filter & MC UV Protection Filter Set for Camera Lens K-Series [[VIDEOID:2b8bb26ef242fcb874bd3c461ac0e558]] For the price, this is a decent circular polarizing filter for amateurs who want to get into using a polarizing filter. It includes a UV filter that I consider just an extra.

I personally don't recommend the use of UV filters unless you are shooting film, as they generally don't improve image quality on modern digital cameras and, if anything, can only degrade it. I know that a lot of people consider them a layer of protection for their expensive lenses, but I am of the opinion that having a cheap UV filter on your expensive lens is actually more likely to damage it. Case in point, the threads on this filter are very sharply cut. You can feel and hear them grinding when you screw it into place, and when it is tightened down snug, the sharp threads want to lock it into place. If the lens was knocked hard on the corner with the filter in this position, the UV filter might actually become stuck in place and damage the threads of the lens, requiring expert repairs to remove the filter and repair the lens. In my experience, just keeping the lens hood in place offers far more protection than a UV filter possibly could.

With that out of the way, let's get to the meat of this review, which is the CPL filter. For the price, this will perform perfectly well. It will darken the sky when used properly in the right conditions, and can help reduce glare and reflections. It seems to have no discernible color cast which would be a problem. In fact the only real issue I have with this filter is related to the mechanical function.

First of all, the threads are very sharply cut, as mentioned previously with the UV filter. This isn't the end of the world, but it is coupled by the fact that the rotating ring on the CPL filter is also very, very stiff and resists turning quite a lot. In order to turn it, as is necessary for adjusting it to the present conditions, you will need to tighten the filter down onto your lens more than I would like, and with such sharp threads, this increases the risk of the threads locking firmly onto your lens. It is possible for them to lock so firmly that it could be quite difficult to remove it from your lens. While $30 is a pretty good bargain for what is otherwise a pretty decent filter, it's not such a bargain if it runs the risk of costing you a lot of money in repairs to your expensive gear. If you are using a cheap lens, then this cheap filter should be just fine. If you have shelled out lots of money for an expensive lens, I would not recommend cheaping out on the filters.

In the end I settled on 4 stars because the glass is pretty decent quality, and if you are aware of the limitations you can safely use it so long as you avoid tightening it down too much. It's just a little less convenient. But it otherwise works well.
text_fidelity_b: K&F Concept 49mm UV CPL Lens Filter Kit 18 Multi Layer Coatings Circular Polarizer Filter & MC UV Protection Filter Set for Camera Lens K-Series

text_fidelity_a:
Netvue Indoor Camera, Enhanced Security Camera with Advanced AI Skills for Pet/Baby/Nanny, 1080P FHD 2.4GHz WiFi Night Vision Home Camera, 2-Way Audio Dog Camera Cloud Storage/TF Card, Black This is the third Netvue Camera I purchased. At the time of this review, this Netvue Orb Cam is the same list price as the Netvue Home Cam I previously purchased. Taking into consideration that Netvue Home Cam doesn't have the Pan & Tilt feature that this Cam does, getting added features for the same price is always nice.

Linking this camera to my account was straightforward and easy to do. Also, setup was easier to do than most wifi plugs and wall switches.

My son added my Netvue cameras to my Alexa account and setup Routines so the motion detection turns on lights connected to smart plugs as I walk through the house.

Performance of this Camera matches the quality of my other Netvue Cams and my Ring Doorbell 2 cam.

Pan & Tilt feature is sluggish and does not allow for small adjustment. For me that's not a problem because I won't be changing its angle or position regularly.

As seen in the attached photo, my son installed it at the edge of a window so that the anchor screws went into a stud and the camera wire could be hidden behind a curtain. He moved the surge protector that my cell phone charger and clock plugs into and mounted it on the wall so the camera could be plugged in as it was not long enough to reach the electrical outlet. We had to move furniture around to hide the surge protector.

NOTES:
TO PET OWNERS, if this camera not mounted and is set on a bookcase, the Pan & Tilt feature will not angle down below the level of the item it is sitting on, which means you may not see your pet walking around. I have a German Shepard as a service dog (mobility dog) and I mounted my camera on the wall so I could always see him.

Standard house door is roughly 80" (6' 8") and most home ceiling heights are 8 ft (96") but sometimes 10ft or 12ft. The power cords on all 3 Netvue cameras I own are 6ft (same as a standard household item such as a fan or clock). Every camera has required an extension cord and moving furniture.

I have have read numerous reviews about Smart Home devices complaining they are only 2.4g. 5.0g Wifi has faster transfer speeds but lower reception distances. 2.4g, like this device has, is more reliable with less connection interruptions.
text_fidelity_b: Netvue Indoor Camera, Enhanced Security Camera with Advanced AI Skills for Pet/Baby/Nanny, 1080P FHD 2.4GHz WiFi Night Vision Home Camera, 2-Way Audio Dog Camera Cloud Storage/TF Card, Black

text_fidelity_a:
MUIN Travel Portable Door Lock Device for Home Security and Personal Protection Very clever. And very portable, even though you may want to keep it with the box just because that is built for convenience and storage as well. It won't stop a big guy bent on murdering you, but it will definitely stop a maid from walking in when you're in the bathroom, and give you some peace of mind while you're sleeping.

I travel a lot. And while most chain hotels in the States have a physical lock in addition to the keycard lock which may or may not let a maid in when it's "locked", there are still countless hotels - small and large - overseas that aggravatingly do not have a real physical lock on the doors. I hate that. I hate it a lot, actually, depending on the situation, and this will remedy a lot of issues.

It won't fix sliding doors, so a lot of ryokan and other places with sliding doors will still be an issue. It comes with an extra small rubber piece if your first one should break (it's basically filler for the lock hole).

Really, it's just a sheet metal type thing, but it's a cool design and a great idea. And I'm quite happy with it.

Oh...one time I ended up in this beach house with all kinds of people I didn't even know. I immediately noticed there was no lock on the door and of course some dorky kid (that I didn't know) comes plowing in right away. God, I would have loved to have this thing back then.

You can't use it to lock the door when you're out of the room.

Some might consider it a fire hazard, but I've always been a privacy-and-not-getting-murdered-over-ease-of-fire-fighters-entering-guy any day.
text_fidelity_b: MUIN Travel Portable Door Lock Device for Home Security and Personal Protection

text_fidelity_a:
Motorola CommandOne Bluetooth Headset - Retail Packaging One of the most important attributes for a headset is comfort. I've tried a few over the years, but always have found them to be a pain (literally!) if they are worn for more than 20 minutes or so. I'm very happy to report that the Moto is a dream when it comes to comfort - had it on for a three+ hour drive, and didn't even know it was there. Plus, it didn't cause a problem with my glasses, unlike other models I've tried.

Set up was very straightforward - basically just follow the prompts and it works. I didn't try out the text-to-voice feature but it sounds interesting. Not really something I would use since I don't text much at all, but if you're text-heavy, that feature would certainly be of value.

Audio quality was excellent. Had no problems hearing callers even with music playing in the car. Range was also very good.

My complaints are two-fold. First a minor one - this comes packed in what I would consider to be wasteful packaging. Looks impressive in a clear, thick plastic box, but the amount of materials used for packing is unnecessary. I did not, however, deduct anything from its rating due to that.

What did cause a loss of one star was the mic pickup. In a quiet environment it was fine. But, in a noisy environment (such as outside, in a crowded restaurant or with moderate-level music playing in the car), it picks up so much background noise that people had problems hearing me. To ensure this was actually the case, I loaned it to a friend and had him call me so I could hear for myself. It seems that the mic is either way too sensitive or not sufficiently directional - it truly is hard to hear the person's voice when they are using the headset should they be in anything other than a pretty quiet environment..

But, that aside, this is the best headset I've used to date. Especially recommended if you have had comfort issues with other headsets or are a glasses wearer.
text_fidelity_b: Motorola CommandOne Bluetooth Headset - Retail Packaging

text_fidelity_a:
Vantrue N2 Pro Uber Dual Dash Cam Infrared Night Vision, Dual Channel 1080P Front and Inside Dash Cam, 2.5K Single Front Car Accident Dash Camera, 24hr Motion Sensor Parking Mode, Support 256GB max I upgraded from a previous Vantrue X3 dash camera which I really liked. The nightvision on the X3 was already really good but the improvement of the nightvision on this N2 pro is significant.

The mount on the N2 pro is similar to other Vantrue mounts but seems a little sturdier in quality. It holds the camera nicely and can be adjusted and doesn't seem overly loose in adjustment like my previous X3 mount.

The build quality on the N2 pro feels really sturdy and is top notch.
The dual (internal facing) camera really needs to be positioned in the center of the dash window to get a good field of view internally. This could be a restriction for some car mounts as people may not want it right in the middle of their windshield. Recording can be set to record both external (street view) and internal (passenger view) at the same time, it can also be set for external view only and multiple resolutions at that for those that want privacy. GPS is an option but requires a separate product addon.

The SD card slot is hidden behind a plastic cover on the side of the camera. This wasn't super intuitive for me to figure out (I admittedly didn't read the manual...) but it is a nice improvement as it adds an extra layer of protection from incidents in which the SD card falls out accidentally.

I live in a hot and humid climate and the X3 mount would occasionally fall off my dash window every few months. Time will tell how this N2 mount will hold up. That being said, the suction cup mount, in general, is a huge improvement over other vendors' camera's sticky tape type mounts which never hold up for more than a week in my climate.

I really like this dash camera and would buy it again if I were in the market for a quality one.
text_fidelity_b: Vantrue N2 Pro Uber Dual Dash Cam Infrared Night Vision, Dual Channel 1080P Front and Inside Dash Cam, 2.5K Single Front Car Accident Dash Camera, 24hr Motion Sensor Parking Mode, Support 256GB max

I'm VERY very very OCD about my screen protectors, and the unique wet application of this one makes it an absolute joy to apply and to use.

The instructions are very easy to follow, all you need is in the kit.

So you spray the spray stuff on, slide the shield around until it's where you want it, then squeegee it down and let it sit. For me, the iPad was completely useable immediately.

What's even better is, a few months later, the corners were lifting and getting some grit under them (not a flaw in the shield ... I was using this with an iPad cover whose silicone covers move a little and shove the shield up). I pulled the corners up, sprayed the solution on (they send way more than you need for one application), flicked off the grit, squeegeed it back down ... good as new!

Given the flexible nature of the film I think a lot of devices that get a lot of rubbing at the edges might get this peeling effect, but it's great how keeping that bottle of spray around lets you fix it right up. When I peeled the corner back i accidentally touched some tissue to the guard, and it stuck to it, and I thought I was done for ... but spraying the liquid solution on, the tissue let go and like I said, it went back down at the corners as good as new.

I'll absolutely be buying these for all future big electronic purchases.

text_fidelity_a:
Garmin nüvi 55LM GPS Navigator System with Spoken Turn-By-Turn Directions, Preloaded Maps and Speed Limit Displays (Discontinued by Manufacturer The story is not good here... Took this brand new, updated Garmin 55LM on a trip drive around Vermont and New Hampshire last week.
The Bad:
1) WORST: We were taken off a main road onto a loop of several miles (usually dirt) that then took us back to the main road we were originally on. Crazy, senseless driving directions. Had it set on fastest route. This happened several times, not just once. (Sadly, we were unable to find a map of NH & so had to rely on the Garmin.)
2) Had it set to avoid dirt roads - it didn't, often sending us down obscure and unnecessary back roads.
3) The announcement of where to turn is dicey at best. Sometimes it told us before the road, sometimes it made its announcement AT the turn, and sometimes it didn't speak up until AFTER the turn.
4) "Recalculating" is gone. GONE! I always relied on that to let me know if I'd made a mistake and/or to have it acknowledged when I was changing the route on the fly. Maybe there's a way to turn it back on, but I haven't found it yet.
5) No choice that I could find for American male voice - just two females. I LIKE the male voice.
6) It pretty much refused to route us to four-lane highways for short stretches of a few miles, preferring all manner of roundabout back roads and streets with an infinite number of turns, even though the highway would have saved lots of time.

I do like some of the software features that are new since my old one, hence I didn't give it a one star rating. Nice overview of the whole trip. But there are some serious problems here. Maybe this device would be fine in a larger urban area. It wasted LOTS of time and led to terrible aggravation in rural areas, though.
text_fidelity_b: Garmin nüvi 55LM GPS Navigator System with Spoken Turn-By-Turn Directions, Preloaded Maps and Speed Limit Displays (Discontinued by Manufacturer

Canvas Laptop Backpack Shoulder Bag - College Outdoor - Fit 15" Laptop (Brown) I’m really impressed with this backpack. Given the price point, I was expecting a so-so pack with limited functionality. Instead, this backpack has quite a few well-done features, and the overall appearance is very striking.

It’s made mostly of canvas, which gives is a “broken in” look right from the start. It’s a very nice change from the usual nylon packs. The canvas is thick and sturdy, and has a great feel to it.

The build quality is impressive considering the price. The stitching is all tight and even, the zippers are of good quality, and the snaps/fasteners are all solid and durable. The strap padding is a little thin, but still comfortable. I was really pleased to see that there was padding on the back. That’s not an option I was expecting at this price. It gives the pack a much more comfortable feel when it’s loaded down.

The inside is lined with a smooth, snag-free lining that’s either nylon or poly (not 100% sure). In any case, it is also very well stitched, with no loose threads, sags or puckers in the material. It makes it very easy to slide books, laptops, etc. in and out of the pack. There are also a couple of compartments inside the pack, both zippered and open, to help organize all the little items that everyone needs to tote around. Additional pouches are on the outside of the pack, which are great for easy access. I didn't have any problem stowing all my small items inside of some type of pouch.

The size is ample for a typical laptop plus a few other items. I loaded it down with books to see if it could take the weight, and the pack performed very well.

The build quality, looks and performance make this an excellent value for the price. Well worth considering if you’re looking for a pack that won’t break the bank in terms of cost.

text_fidelity_a:
Samsung SyncMaster 245BW 24-inch LCD Monitor This is the first high quality 24" I have seen for under $500. Yes, this is one of the new 24" TN (twisted neumatic) panels, but don't let that dissuade you. The 22" TN panels have gotten a bad rap due to their poor performance, most of them have issues with bad color banding and lots of light bleeding at the edges. I should know as I have owned several 22" TN panels (mostly Viewsonic VX2235WM).

This 24" TN panel is far and away superior to any previous TN panels I have seen, it is almost laughable how bad my old 22" TN panel looks up next to this one. I would challenge you to put this 24" TN up against any of the more expensive 24" IPS or S-PVA panels and see the difference for yourself, I doubt you will be able to tell which is which unless you are using a specialized image for gamut testing or you are a graphic designer with an extremely keen eye.

The only downsides that some people may find with this monitor compared to other (usually more expensive) 24" panels are: less inputs, no portrait mode. This monitor only has VGA and DVI(+hdcp) inputs, no component or hdmi, this is not really an issue if you are using it as a computer monitor but may turn off some people who wish to hook up other media devices. Also there is no portrait mode like the other 24" samsung 244T series; however, the stand on this monitor is still extremely high quality and height adjustable.

I would very highly recommend this LCD, better yet, I'd recommend 2 or 3. Why buy a 30" when you could have 3 of these for the same price?!
text_fidelity_b: Samsung SyncMaster 245BW 24-inch LCD Monitor

I always like my electronics to have buttons and especially my kindle since I tend to read with one thumb on the screen itself I worried that if I upgraded to this, my thumb would either end up turning pages too soon or it wouldn't be sensitive enough to read my thumb when I wanted to. My old kindle no longer took a charge after 6 years so I had to upgrade and literally the only reason I went with this over anything else (I was wanting to get another one of my old kindles) was the backlight. I have insomnia so I'm often awake in bed with my snoring boyfriend next to me so having a light on isn't an option so having a kindle with a backlight would be ideal.

Turns out my worry over not having a button was all in vain! The touch screen has just the right amount of sensitivity. It's not so sensitive that resting my thumb on the screen where it's comfortable activates anything, but it's not so dull that I can't turn the pages easily. The back lighting is adjustable so I don't have to blind myself and I don't have to use it if I don't want to if I've got plenty of natural light. The screen is clear and crisp, it fits comfortably in my hand and the amount of books I can fit on there is insane! I've currently got 200 titles and I've still got plenty of room for more. It moves faster than my old kindle and the charge is amazing. I've been using it for over a month now and I'm still at 25% battery without charging it once aside from the day I received it.

This is by far the best kindle I've ever had!
text_fidelity_b: Kindle Paperwhite E-reader (Previous Generation - 2015 release) - White, 6" High-Resolution Display (300 ppi) with Built-in Light, Wi-Fi, Ad-Supported

text_fidelity_a:
Panasonic DMP-BD87 Ultra-Fast Booting Blu-ray Disc Player When we first tried it, the streaming was awful. It couldn't hold a connection to Vudu, to Hulu, or to Netflix.

We ran an update--tricky because it didn't readily hold a solid network connection--and things improved considerably. I can stream Hulu with minor hiccups, Netflix without issues, and Vudu except at 1080p. For the record, I can stream Vudu at 1080p on the TV that the player is connected to. It still supports only a small subset of services, though Hulu has been added. As a streaming media player, it doesn't meet expectations. As a simple blu-ray player, it is quite excellent for the price. It was able to play a few old, slightly scratched DVDs that other players were having trouble loading.

On the signature features, I could find no appreciable difference in boot up or launch time between this and my Sony, or between this with fast boot turned on and this with fast boot turned off. Blu-ray players tend to boot pretty fast in any case. This one allows up to four users to have customized interfaces, but it only affects the background image and color scheme of the interface screen. It does not allow four users to each maintain their own login to Netflix or Hulu, which would be useful if Netflix ever allowed multiple users of an account to maintain their own Watch Instantly queue the way they do with DVD queues.
text_fidelity_b: Panasonic DMP-BD87 Ultra-Fast Booting Blu-ray Disc Player

Polk Audio ES35 Sound Wall Mount Speakers, Black & Polk Audio ES15 Wall Mount Bookshelf Speaker, Black I'm very pleased with all aspects of this center speaker. The sound quality is excellent. This replaces an old KEF center speaker and the difference can be clearly heard. The Polk has a crisp, clean sound that clarifies and enhances dialog but not at the expense of a nice solid bass (although I also have a subwoofer in the setup).

Aesthetically it's a simple, clean design. Normally I don't pay much attention to the look of a speaker but in this case, since it's a center speaker, it's in my line of sight all the time. It's about as unobtrusive you can get with a center speaker without compromising sound quality and performance. Polk did an excellent job with the design.

I looked at the new version of this (the ES35) and, while there are some small incremental improvements, I didn't consider them to be worth the extra $100 it costs. Plus, this was on a price dip for the differential between the two was $150, making this the clear choice.

While I have been partial to KEF in the past for speakers, the performance of this Polk has really wow'd me. At present I'm using this center speaker with KEF left and right front speakers, and KEF for surround. I've been so impressed with the ES35 that I'll be changing to Polk for my L/R soon, and keep the KEF only for surround (5.1.2 setup).

An excellent center speaker that hits the mark on all counts. Five stars.
text_fidelity_b: Polk Audio ES35 Sound Wall Mount Speakers, Black & Polk Audio ES15 Wall Mount Bookshelf Speaker, Black

text_fidelity_a:
Luby Portable Movie Projector with Free Projector Screen Perfect for Fun Camping Neighborhood Gathering Backyard Movie The listing says this projector supports 1920 X 1080p resolution. It doesn't say it projects in that resolution. And it doesn't. You can see the pixel grid on the home screen. It's definitely not a 1080p projector. I don't even think it's 720p. Text is pretty blurry when you connect it to a computer as a monitor. If you do that, you might want to enlarge the font for readability.

Brightness is pretty good. It's better than mini projectors I've seen in the past. But the room (or outdoors, if you're using it there) will need to be pretty dark to get a good view. The farther away the projector is from the screen, the bigger the picture, the more spread out the light is, the darker the room will need to be to see it.

I had hopes the OS would play DVDs directly from a USB-powered outboard DVD player, but it doesn't have that functionality. I tried it and it would not recognize the connected device. You do have to manually select the input from the home screen. There are multiple inputs: HDMI, VGA, micro SD card, and USB.

The included screen is okay, but a white wall (or even ceiling) works well too.

On the bottom of the projector is a tripod mounting hole, a nice addition.

The manual keystone adjustment works only for up and down adjustment, not side to side. The focus is also manual, and works well.

The two negatives to me are that the remote control pretty much has to be aimed directly at the IR receiver ports on the projector to get it to work (there are ports on the front and back), and there is some trash inside the lens that shows up in the projected image in the one I received. I'll have to open up the projector to blow that out.

Other than that, at this price point, it's a good projector, and pretty versatile in terms of portability and input options.
text_fidelity_b: Luby Portable Movie Projector with Free Projector Screen Perfect for Fun Camping Neighborhood Gathering Backyard Movie

Etymotic Research MC5 Noise-Isolating In-Ear Earphones I bought these to supplement my ER6i phones which I enjoy and have had no problems with. Unfortunately, they are no longer made so I bought these which I felt would be equivalent. That turned out to not be the case. The sound isolation is lacking, no matter how far they are jammed into my ear canals - it seems they may be purposely letting in some med/high end frequencies to give the phones a more open sound. In my case it seems to heighten certain ambient noises I am interested in blocking - running fans especially. Microphony from the dangling cables seems to be more noticeable too.

These guys have to absolutely invade my ear canals whereas the ER6i phones would need to just barely enter my ear to make a seal. The result is very noticeable and eventually uncomfortable.

The wires are thicker which seems nice at first, but they just get in the way - the thinner wires of the ER6i would pretty much fall into place and not be a nuisance.

All in all, I could tell these were unacceptable within a half hour of use and they are going back.

text_fidelity_a:
OCTA Spider Monkey - Secure Height Adjustable Stand for iPad, Galaxy, Surface and All Tablets for Desk, Bed, Car, Couch Do I like the Spider Monkey? Yes... with reservations. First let me cover why I like it. I read in bed, and I spend a lot of time switching hands, trying to find ways to prop my book or tablet up, shaking feeling back into my fingers. And then, when I fall asleep, which I always do, the tablet might end up under me or might end up on the floor, and neither is good. The Spider Monkey gives me a way to prop up my tablet without holding it, and to keep it out of my way when I fall asleep.

The downside? How it works depends very much on what you attach it to. I have a headboard that allows me to twist and anchor the tail in a lot of ways, but it doesn't always hold the tablet in position. It can swing around, and be difficult to angle for good reading. Also? It's not all that easy to put together. Once you do, it'll hold, but until then you may find yourself screaming in frustration.

In spite of the drawbacks, though, the Spider Monkey has been a real boon to my reading. If I work with it a bit, it'll even hold my kindle in its cover. I'm not sure I think it's worth $80, to be honest. Half that seems fair to me.

Disclaimer: I received this product in exchange for an honest review.
text_fidelity_b: OCTA Spider Monkey - Secure Height Adjustable Stand for iPad, Galaxy, Surface and All Tablets for Desk, Bed, Car, Couch
